thread:
maria (docs): hey team — I'm kicking off a tiny refresh of the onboarding lab used in the hello-min app. goal: make first deploy + auth smooth for new devs, include an env-helper, and a short migration note for v1->v2 tokens. any objections?

tyler (eng): love it. +1 on env helper. can we standardize on REDWOOD_API_URL and REDWOOD_API_KEY env names? saves questions.

maria (docs): yep that's the plan. I'll replace mentions of 'api_host' with REDWOOD_API_URL and add a snippet for bash/fish.

kevin (devex): also add a tiny node snippet for setting env vars locally (cross-platform note). most folks use direnv or just a `.env` file.

maria (docs): good call — will include both. thinking of a one-file helper: `scripts/setup-env.sh` that does `export REDWOOD_API_URL=...` and prints next steps. sample:```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# quick helper for onboarding
export REDWOOD_API_URL=https://api.redwood-inference.example
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=REPLACE_ME
echo "env vars set for this shell. run: node examples/hello.js"
```

tyler (eng): tiny nit — echo should warn if KEY is placeholder. also add comment about not committing `.env`.

maria (docs): will do. also planning a short migration blurb: "If you used v1 tokens, create a new v2 API key in the console; v1 keys are read-only and will be deprecated on 2026-09-01". can someone confirm timeline?

mike (qa): timeline is correct for deprecation notice. we should include a quick-to-run test command to validate a key: `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" $REDWOOD_API_URL/v1/health` -> 200.

kevin (devex): for SDK snippets, show minimal Node and Python examples — keep output handling simple e.g. streaming vs non-streaming note. avoid long examples, link to full sample repo.

maria (docs): drafting two short snippets. node: 5 lines showing `client.generate(...)`. python: same idea. will link to https://github.com/redwood-inference/hello-min for full code. anyone want to volunteer to sanity-check the snippets?

tyler (eng): I can quick review the Node snippet.

mike (qa): I'll run through the whole lab on mac + linux and report any flakiness.

maria (docs): awesome, thanks. opening a docs PR in a few mins: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1234 (WIP). tagging reviewers.

jess-bot: CI: markdown-lint passed. broken link check: 1 warning -> `./old-examples/auth-v1.md` referenced.

maria (docs): thanks bot — I'll remove the v1 doc link and replace with migration note.

tyler (eng): small UX ask — add a one-line troubleshooting section: "If you see 401, check REDWOOD_API_KEY and ensure you didn't paste extra quotes." That saves support messages.

maria (docs): good. final Q: shall we add a tiny browser-based example that uses the hosted API with CORS note? or that's scope creep?

kevin (devex): keep it out for this pass. we can add web example as follow-up with proper guidance on CORS + token exposure.

maria (docs): ok locking this as v1 of the refresh. PR will include: env helper, small migration note, node/python snippets, test curl command, and troubleshooting. tagging reviewers: @tyler (eng) @mike (qa) @kevin (devex). ETA: review request in 1h, docs ship if no blockers. :rocket:
